message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to current air‑quality data, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment.  

**What you can do instead**

| Source | How to use it | What it gives you |
|--------|---------------|-------------------|
| **AirNow (EPA)** | Visit https://www.airnow.gov/ and enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code. | Current AQI, pollutant breakdown (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO, SO₂), forecast for the next 24–48 h. |
| **AQICN (World Air Quality Index)** | Go to https://aqicn.org/city/los-angeles/ | Real‑time AQI, historical trends, health recommendations. |
| **Local news/weather apps** | Many local stations (e.g., KABC, KNBC) publish live air‑quality updates. | Quick visual alerts, health advisories. |
| **Mobile apps** | Apps like “AirVisual”, “Plume Labs: Air Report”, or “EPA AirNow” provide push notifications. | Continuous monitoring, alerts for unhealthy levels. |

**Typical LA air‑quality context**

- Los Angeles often experiences moderate to unhealthy‑for‑sensitive‑groups levels of fine particulate matter (PM₂.₅) and ozone (O₃), especially during late spring and summer.
- Traffic congestion, industrial activity, and regional wildfires can spike pollutant concentrations.
- The city has implemented measures such as low‑emission zones, public‑transport incentives, and stricter vehicle standards to improve air quality over the past decade.

If you’re planning outdoor activities or have respiratory concerns, checking one of the above sources right before you head out will give you the most accurate and actionable information.
